records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — Persisting the safeParse result instead of its data nests Google tokens under data and makes the next credential load fail validation.
records.rationale: The diff changes `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`, and the new helper in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts returns `refreshTokenResponse` — the whole safeParse result object (`{success, data}`), not `.data`. This nested object is then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored credential key no longer matches the googleCredentialSchema shape; on next load, `credential.key` validation against the same schema would fail.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — Substituting the literal refresh_token when an Outlook refresh response omits that optional field overwrites the saved valid token and breaks subsequent refreshes.
records.rationale: The diff shows in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }` — assigning the literal string, not a real token. Office365CalendarService then does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`, overwriting the stored valid refresh_token with that literal, so subsequent refresh calls would send the string 'refresh_token' as the grant and fail. This is a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The any return boundary hides incompatible fetch and SDK responses, breaking Google and HubSpot shared refreshes; normalize both branches to a typed token contract.
records.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens is typed to return any and in the shared-mode branch returns a raw fetch Response, while Google's CalendarService does `const token = res?.data` on the result. A fetch Response has no `.data` property, so when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set the Google refresh path reads `token.access_token` on undefined and throws; similarly HubSpot expects a HubspotToken from the SDK in the non-shared branch but a Response in the shared branch. The untyped `any` boundary genuinely conflates incompatible response shapes across branches introduced by this diff.
